title: W2 fold disposition incomplete: PR body §4 still claims demolish-frees-budget as behavior; balance.json comment never got the promised acknowledgment
evidence:
PR body lines 38-39: "4. **District caps**: `cap(d) = max(1, floor(pool_tiles(d) × permille /
   1000))`, gating BOTH families; demolished terminals free the budget
   (live counts derive from the topology)." — vs the same file's r1-fold section, lines 117-120: "- **W2: demolish-frees-budget acknowledged vacuous-by-design** — E2 forbids
  terminal demolish (validate_demolish_node → .Terminal_Demolish), so the
  live count is monotone within a run; the spec/PR/balance comments now
  say so instead of claiming verified behavior." — while data/balance.json growth_districts._comment (line 22) contains no live-count/demolish/vacuous wording at all (grep for demolish|vacuous|monotone across data/balance.json matches nothing inside growth_districts), and the spec does carry it (spec-v2-dublin-spawn-director.md:118 "the freeing clause is vacuous-by-design"). .memlog.md:5 makes the same claim: "W2 ... -> acknowledged vacuous-by-design in spec/PR/balance comments."
detail: The fold claims the W2 acknowledgment landed in spec/PR/balance comments; it landed only in the spec and the fold section. The PR body's own §4 still asserts the r1-flagged vacuous behavior unqualified, and balance.json's growth_districts comment never mentions it.
recommended_fix: Qualify PR body §4 ("demolished terminals free the budget" → add "vacuous-by-design under E2 — count is monotone") and add the live-count/demolish note to balance.json's growth_districts _comment.

title: dublin_board.dem claims router tile (20,15) is a pool tile; it is not in the 603-tile stride-6 pool
evidence:
demos/dublin_board.dem:17-18: "# The mesh: two high routers on the city core's street tiles ((20,15) + (16,12)
# are pool tiles near Temple Bar / the Liffey) joined by a wide fiber — the". Independent replication of the loader (core/map.odin:366-397: stride 6 over spawn_candidates, f32 snap with C-style math.round, 40×30 grid filter, first-occurrence dedupe) reproduces the committed census EXACTLY (spawn-audit.txt:2 "census pool=603 (city 5, town 7, village 0, suburb 517, quarter 18, neighbourhood 56)" plus all 14 per-district pool= values), and (20,15) is NOT among the 603: every asset candidate snapping to (20,15) (e.g. index 109183 (19.52, 15.12)) sits at a non-stride-6 index; (16,12) IS a pool tile (stride-6 candidate index 94500 (15.80, 12.38)).
detail: Half the claim is false: (20,15) is not a spawn-pool tile. Harmless to behavior (routers are player-placed, not pool-drawn), but the golden demo's header misstates the asset the chunk's other evidence leans on.
recommended_fix: Reword the demo comment (e.g. "street-adjacent core tiles near the Liffey"), or name only (16,12) as a pool tile, or move the router onto an actual pool tile if the claim should hold.

title: growth_test one-tile-district fixture hand-builds district_tiles instead of calling the shared map_board_partition
evidence:
core/growth_test.odin:1124-1130 (test_growth_district_seed_draw_cap_and_exhaustion): "	one: Map_Board
	one.w_tiles = 40
	one.h_tiles = 30
	append(&one.districts, Map_District{name = "A", kind = .City, pos = {6, 6}})
	append(&one.candidates, [2]i32{1, 1})
	one.district_tiles = make([dynamic][dynamic]u32, 1, 1, context.temp_allocator)
	append(&one.district_tiles[0], 0)" — versus the stated contract at core/map.odin:414-416: "// the loader and every test fixture call map_board_partition, so the / assignment can never drift between them" and .memlog.md:5's "shared map_board_partition builder (loader + all fixtures — one definition)". All other fixtures (map_test.odin:53, 306, 333, 579, 635, 683) and the loader (map.odin:417) call the builder.
detail: One partition-build site still bypasses the shared builder the fold claims is universal. Identical output today, but a future partition change (tie-break, scaling) silently diverges this fixture from the loader.
recommended_fix: Replace the two hand-built lines with map_board_partition(&one, context.temp_allocator) after appending the candidate — produces the identical [[0]] partition.
